title: The Thundering Coast
dek: Prima’s shore beyond Eovar: ranchers, the offshore beacon, a hidden landing and the unresolved wreck of the Looking Glass.

facts.Recorded routes: Eovar approach; landing cove and hunter’s path to Pristinia

sources: Quest narrator · harbor/coast approach, posted 13 March 2024 · https://discord.com/channels/1177270231513694249/1199083630354501673/1217654903535702158
Quest narrator · beacon beyond the coast, posted 27 May 2024 · https://discord.com/channels/1177270231513694249/1199083630354501673/1244736241862311958
body:
The Thundering Coast belongs to Prima. It appears in the adventurers’ approach to Eovar Harbor and in the preparations for a voyage toward a light beyond the coast.

Its history includes the ranchers sought for Pristinia’s work animals, an offshore light that draws a company to Eovar, a discreet landing on the way home and a wreck whose investigation leaves more questions than the first fight answers. These are separate visits to a stretch of Prima’s shore.

13 March 2024 · the harbor comes into view

After breaking a trap on the road to Eovar, Jiangshi, Scribonia, Rolen, John, Adelia and Forgax reach the final hill overlooking the harbor and the Thundering Coast.

Horses for a growing town

Scout Lilian directs the town’s would-be horse buyers toward the coast. The ranchers, she says, graze their herds there and keep horses. The conversation begins with Pristinia’s practical needs: hauling wood and stone, farming and forming a mounted defense.

Rolen wants an arrangement with the ranchers and offers to contribute his own money. Vigr also offers funds. Cobble worries about taking someone else’s horses, then agrees that paying would be better. They debate how many mounts and draft animals a young settlement can support. The coast is part of their hoped-for supply route; this discussion alone does not establish a completed purchase.

27 May 2024 · passage toward the light

With Eovar’s quarantine lifted, Olokun, Loistava, Nienna, Adelia, Bari and Alyhotep seek passage at the docks toward the beacon shining beyond the Thundering Coast. The harbor reconnects the party to sailors, ships and travel beyond the shore.

The port’s improved mood follows the lifting of quarantine. Nienna brings the money and asks Olokun to judge the boats. Bari worries about room for the company and his horse; Olokun considers a vessel large enough for the passengers but manageable in shallow water. Adelia urges them to be ready for danger. Reaching the docks is the beginning of arranging passage, rather than proof that the company has already reached the light.

A way home beside the harbor

On a later return to Prima, Quake and the company need somewhere to land without drawing Eovar’s attention. Their captain proposes a small cove beside the Thundering Coast and a hunter’s path leading to Pristinia. The sailors will remain with the ship rather than enter the town.

Quake accepts. Within two hours the travelers are ready in rowboats. Saray thanks the captain for staying with them despite the risk; he answers by recalling their help to his people. As the sun lowers, the company takes the trail and reaches Pristinia, where friends are waiting. The landing supplies a concrete route between coast and settlement, without placing every nearby site inside Eovar Harbor.

The Looking Glass on the rocks

A much later investigation begins with stories about the sea around Eovar. Fisherman Nico offers possibilities rather than an answer: something large, a storm, perhaps a dragon. He points the company toward the wreck of the Looking Glass on the Thundering Coast. When Frod asks for the safest way there, Maartje directs them out of the main gate toward the rocky shore.

The guards release Chesire to accompany the company, and the narrator explicitly places the wreck on this coast. Harpies are picking through its scraps. Frod hopes to begin with a captain’s log and a manifest, but the encounter becomes a fight before the wreck can be searched in peace.

Di’trillio draws an attacker toward him. A harpy’s song overwhelms Yuna and Velkyn for a time; Frod initially retreats into his shell before forcing himself back into the fight. His grease and Velkyn’s fire turn the struggle, but the resulting suffering horrifies Frod. The surviving harpies flee. Their presence on the beach does not establish that they sank the ship or caused the storms.

Inside the captain’s quarters, Frod and Velkyn find a journal. Other searchers discover claw marks concentrated around a chest and examine an occult object found there. The assessment is limited: it might be protective, or it might be a beacon. Di’trillio wraps it in cloth rather than handling it casually. The checked scene ends with evidence to investigate, not a solved account of the wreck or the sea’s danger.

The routes that can be followed

The hill above Eovar, the ranchers’ reported grazing land, the captain’s landing cove and the rocky wreck site give the coast several connections to the people of Prima. None supplies a complete shoreline chart. The hunter’s path leads toward Pristinia; the port remains the place where the beacon company seeks a vessel.

The coast’s exact boundaries and the beacon’s precise position remain unconfirmed.
